# New-ZbxCepRule

## SYNOPSIS

Creates an event processing rule.

## SYNTAX

```
New-ZbxCepRule [[-Name] <string>] [[-Position] <int>] [-Filter <ZabbixCepRuleFilterRequest>] [-WindowType <ZabbixCepRuleWindowType>] [-Window <ZabbixCepRuleWindowRequest>] [-Operation <ZabbixCepRuleOperationRequest[]>] [-Stop <ZabbixCepRuleExecution>] [-Description <string>] [-Status <ZabbixCepRuleStatus>] [-AdditionalProperty <Hashtable>] [-Force] [-InputObject <PSObject>] [-Connection <ZabbixConnection>] [-WhatIf] [-Confirm] [<CommonParameters>]
```

## DESCRIPTION

An event processing rule matches incoming events against a filter within a time window and applies its operations to them, in sort order (Zabbix 8.0 and later). The New-ZbxCepRule cmdlet sends ceprule.create with one request field per parameter, then reads the new event processing rule back with ceprule.get and writes it. The server requires -Name and -Position; -AdditionalProperty sets any other field by its API name and wins over a parameter. -WhatIf shows what would be created, and the command needs a connection made with Connect-ZbxServer.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1: Create an event processing rule

```powershell
New-ZbxCepRule -Name 'Tag web alerts' -Position 1 -Description 'Tags the alerts of the web tier' -Operation @{ sortorder = 1; execute_when = 0; type = 11; tag = 'tier'; tag_value = 'web' }
```

Creates an event processing rule named Tag web alerts. The operation adds the tag tier=web to every event the rule sees (type 11 adds a tag; execute_when 0 runs it when the event occurs); the command writes the new rule, read back from the server.
